answers.answer: Use the channel helpers. They always read the broadcaster's channel: {channel} for the login name, {channel.display} for the display name, {channel.mention} for an @mention and {channel.id} for the Twitch ID. They take no arguments. Only the two raid counts take an input, which is a login name after a colon.
answers.quote: Every helper on this page reads your channel, never the person who triggered the reply.

answers.answer: You need to know how braces work and which fields take them, from the Variables and templates page, which the first paragraph names. Viewer-typed text also needs the Viewer Templates feature and the template permission, which the Name and ID section states.
answers.quote: For how braces work and which fields take them, read Variables and templates first.

answers.answer: It worked when a moderator runs the command and the reply names the broadcaster's channel, not the moderator's. A helper that cannot resolve prints as typed, braces and all. A few, such as {channel.tags}, give empty text instead.
answers.quote: When a moderator runs a command with {channel} in it, the reply names your channel, not the moderator’s.

answers.answer: Put the example reply in the command. {channel} gives the broadcaster's login name, so the link points to the broadcaster's channel whichever moderator runs it. {channel.url} cannot be used because it works only in a Discord notification. For Kick, use {platform.link.kick} instead.

The page says the helpers that give empty text say so in their rows. But the {channel.url} row in the Discord table does not say it is empty on other platforms; that comes only in the last paragraph. I also learned only at the end that using a Discord-only helper in a command stops the command from saving. The cost is a reread, not a blocked task.
answers.quote: A few helpers give empty text instead, and their rows say so.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the raid helper names with colons and dotted parts are hard to follow. The ccls row's bracketed expansion breaks the sentence. The cost is a slower listen, not a wrong action.
answers.quote: Your channel’s content labels (ccls is short for content classification labels), separated by commas, empty when you have none

warning_review.reason: The five sentences each state one part of the rule: the feature must be on, the viewer needs the template permission, and everyone else sees the text as typed. A reader who wants viewers to use these helpers needs all of them. The sentence count alone is not a defect.

The sentences give the input format (a colon and the other login name), the zero and unknown-name results, and the print-as-typed fallback. A moderator writing a raid count needs each one to know what the reply will show. The length costs little.
